items.text: Business Standard, Jerusalem Post, The Federal (June 11): US Central Command identified the vessel as the Palau-flagged MT Settebello, intercepted in the Gulf of Oman on June 9, alleging it was attempting to move Iranian oil in violation of maritime restrictions. CENTCOM said it 'fired precision munitions into the ship's engine room after the crew repeatedly failed to comply with directions issued by US forces,' rendering it inoperable. Three of the 24 Indian sailors aboard were killed: Aditya Sharma (deck cadet), Shivanand Chaurashiya (engine fitter), and Patnala Suresh (chief engineer). The remaining 25 crew — 21 Indians, 2 Pakistanis, 1 Russian, 1 Ukrainian — were evacuated by the Omani Navy after an engine fire and distress call. These are the first reported deaths since the US blockade on Iran-linked shipping began April 13 — operations that have so far disabled 8 ships and turned back over 100. Aditya Sharma's father told media his son was due home in May but his duty was extended; he is demanding an inquiry into the captain's decision to take the ship close to the Strait of Hormuz.

items.bold: SECOND VESSEL MT JALVEER ATTACKED June 11 — all 20 Indians safely evacuated. THIRD attack on a vessel carrying Indian sailors in 4 days. India Foreign Ministry confirmed both incidents were US Navy actions.
items.text: Tribune India, The Federal (June 11): Just a day after the Settebello strike, the merchant vessel MT Jalveer — carrying 20 Indian crew — came under attack by the US Navy off the coast of Oman. All 20 Indians aboard were safely evacuated. The Indian government confirmed all three recent incidents involving vessels with Indian sailors were the result of US Navy actions enforcing the Hormuz blockade. This represents an unprecedented situation: India's casualties and near-misses are now coming from the US-led blockade enforcement, not from Iranian strikes — a significant complication for India's diplomatic positioning, since the US is a strategic partner, not an adversary in this conflict.

items.bold: MEA SUMMONED US CHARGE D'AFFAIRES Jason Meeks, handed formal demarche/protest note. 'We lodged a strong protest with the American side' — MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. India to raise issue at G7 Evian-les-Bains June 15-17.
items.text: The Tribune, The Federal (June 11): Following the Settebello attack, the Ministry of External Affairs summoned US Chargé d'Affaires Jason Meeks and handed him a demarche — a formal diplomatic note of protest. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated at an inter-ministerial briefing: 'We attach high importance to the welfare and well-being of our seafaring community. When this particular attack on the ship MT Settebello occurred, we lodged a strong protest with the American side... We summoned the US Chargé d'Affaires and he was conveyed our deepest concern over the ongoing incidents of attacks. We also registered our strong protest.' India confirmed the affected ships were foreign-flagged (Palau), not India-owned. Business Standard reports India will raise the issue of attacks on merchant vessels at the G7 summit in Evian-les-Bains, France (June 15-17), which PM Modi will attend — sources say a bilateral meeting with President Trump is likely on the sidelines.

items.text: Business Standard, The Federal (June 11): Officials confirmed that more than 18,000 Indian seafarers remain across the broader Gulf region, including 562 crew members aboard 13 Indian-flagged ships — 329 on vessels west of the Strait of Hormuz and 233 in the Gulf of Oman, east of Hormuz. The Seamen Welfare Fund Society has been directed to pay approximately Rs10 lakh compensation to each deceased sailor's family. This is the first time in the conflict that Indian deaths have resulted directly from US enforcement action rather than Iranian attacks (the June 3 Kuwait airport death and earlier Hormuz casualties were Iranian-attributed). The scale of remaining exposure — 562 Indian crew on Indian-flagged vessels alone, plus 18,000 in the wider region — means further incidents remain a live risk as the blockade-enforcement campaign continues alongside the Iran-US military exchanges.

items.text: RFE/RL live, Trading Economics (June 10-11): Following Tuesday's Apache-response strikes, the US military launched a second consecutive night of strikes against Iran. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported several explosions around the Bandar Abbas airport and airbase, and confirmed 'enemy shells hit a target in Sirik,' a southern port city home to a naval base. Iran retaliated by targeting US military facilities in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait — though some reports of US vessels being attacked in the Strait could not be verified. Separately, an Iranian cargo vessel sank in the Gulf of Oman on June 11 after being struck by a projectile 5 miles from Khasab port (Oman) — all 5 crew rescued and transferred to Oman. Brent climbed toward $95 Thursday, extending gains, on fears that peace efforts could collapse with the conflict dragging on.

items.text: RFE/RL live (June 10): Trump said Iran's military has been 'completely defeated,' warning Tehran would 'pay the price' for taking 'too long to negotiate a deal' with Washington — a marked hardening from Tuesday's 'two or three days' optimism and Vance's 'very close to a deal' framing. Separately, the IAEA's 35-nation board of governors approved a US-backed resolution demanding Iran declare its remaining enriched uranium stockpile and allow IAEA inspectors into the country — adding a new diplomatic pressure track. A Qatari negotiating team reportedly traveled to Tehran on June 10 to address the escalating tensions, indicating that despite Trump's hardened rhetoric and the second night of strikes, diplomatic channels remain active. The juxtaposition — Trump's harshest language yet ('completely defeated,' 'pay the price') alongside active Qatari mediation — suggests negotiating positions are hardening even as the diplomatic track continues.

military.t: 3 INDIAN SAILORS KILLED — US Navy Struck MT Settebello in Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM Fired Precision Munitions into Engine Room. First Blockade-Enforcement Deaths Since April 13. MEA Protests to US.
military.d: Business Standard, Jerusalem Post, The Federal (June 11): US Central Command identified the Palau-flagged tanker MT Settebello as the vessel struck on June 9-10 in the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM said the ship was intercepted while 'attempting to move Iranian oil in violation of the maritime restrictions currently in place,' and that 'an aircraft carried out a precision strike on the Palau-flagged oil products tanker' after 'the crew repeatedly failed to comply with directions issued by American forces' — firing precision munitions into the ship's engine room and rendering it inoperable. Of 24 sailors aboard (21 Indian, 2 Pakistani, 1 Russian, 1 Ukrainian), three Indians were killed: Aditya Sharma (deck cadet), Shivanand Chaurashiya (engine fitter), and Patnala Suresh (chief engineer). The remaining 25 were evacuated by the Omani Navy following an engine-room fire and distress call. These are the first reported fatalities since the US blockade on Iran-linked shipping began April 13 — a campaign that has so far disabled 8 ships and turned back over 100. Aditya Sharma's father said his son's tour had been extended past its scheduled May return and demanded an inquiry into why the captain steered the ship near the Strait.

military.t: MT JALVEER ALSO ATTACKED June 11 — All 20 Indians Safely Evacuated. Third Attack on a Vessel with Indian Sailors in 4 Days. MEA Summoned US Charge d'Affaires Jason Meeks, Lodged Formal Demarche.
military.d: Tribune India, The Federal (June 11): A day after the Settebello strike, the merchant vessel MT Jalveer — carrying 20 Indian crew members — came under attack by the US Navy off the coast of Oman. All 20 Indians aboard were safely evacuated. The Indian government confirmed all three recent incidents involving vessels carrying Indian sailors resulted from US Navy actions enforcing the Hormuz blockade — not Iranian attacks. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal: 'We attach high importance to the welfare and well-being of our seafaring community... We summoned the US Chargé d'Affaires and he was conveyed our deepest concern over the ongoing incidents of attacks. We also registered our strong protest.' The MEA confirmed the affected vessels were foreign-flagged (Palau), not India-owned, but with majority-Indian crews. India will raise the pattern of attacks on merchant vessels at the G7 Summit in Evian-les-Bains (June 15-17), where PM Modi will attend and a bilateral with President Trump is reportedly likely.

military.t: US LAUNCHED 2ND NIGHT OF STRIKES on Iran — Bandar Abbas Airport/Airbase + Sirik Naval Base Hit. Iran Retaliated at Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait. Iranian Cargo Ship Sank in Gulf of Oman (5 Rescued).
military.d: RFE/RL live updates (June 10-11): Following Tuesday's Apache-retaliation strikes, the US military launched a second consecutive night of strikes against Iran. Iran's state news agency IRNA reported multiple explosions around Bandar Abbas airport and airbase, and confirmed 'enemy shells hit a target in Sirik,' a southern naval base port city. Iran retaliated by targeting US military facilities in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait — some reports of attacks on US vessels in the Strait could not be independently verified. Separately, an Iranian cargo vessel departing Khasab (Oman) for Sirik County sank in the Gulf of Oman on June 11 after being struck by a projectile 5 miles from Khasab port — all 5 crew were rescued by passing vessels and transferred to Oman; video showed crew disembarking, with one person describing a drone strike. Brent crude, which had eased to ~$91 on Wednesday on relief hopes, climbed toward $95 on Thursday on fears the conflict could drag on.

military.t: TRUMP: Iran's Military 'Completely Defeated' — Tehran Will 'Pay the Price' for Stalling. IAEA 35-Nation Board Demands Iran Declare Uranium Stockpile + Allow Inspectors. Qatari Team in Tehran.
military.d: RFE/RL live updates (June 10): Trump issued his hardest rhetoric of the week, declaring Iran's military 'completely defeated' and warning Tehran would 'pay the price' for taking 'too long to negotiate a deal' with Washington — a sharp escalation from Tuesday's 'two or three days' and Vance's 'very close to a deal' framing. Separately, the IAEA's 35-nation board of governors approved a US-backed resolution demanding Iran declare its remaining stockpile of enriched uranium and allow IAEA inspectors into the country — opening a new diplomatic pressure track independent of the military exchanges. Despite all this, a Qatari negotiating team reportedly traveled to Tehran on June 10 to address the escalating tensions — diplomacy continues even as rhetoric hardens. assessment.body:
Wednesday 10:30 PM IST. Day 102.
India's darkest day of the 102-day war.

THE TRAGEDY
US Navy struck the Palau-flagged tanker MT Settebello in the Gulf of Oman.
CENTCOM: crew "repeatedly failed to comply" — fired precision munitions
into the engine room, rendering it inoperable.
3 of 24 Indian sailors killed:
  Aditya Sharma — deck cadet
  Shivanand Chaurashiya — engine fitter
  Patnala Suresh — chief engineer
21 Indians + 2 Pakistanis + 1 Russian + 1 Ukrainian evacuated by Oman Navy.
First deaths of the US blockade since it began April 13.
8 ships disabled, 100+ turned back in that period — zero deaths until today.

THE SECOND INCIDENT
A day later, MT Jalveer — 20 Indian crew — also attacked by US Navy.
All 20 safely evacuated.
Third attack on a vessel with Indian sailors in 4 days.

THE DIPLOMATIC COMPLEXITY
India has summoned the US Charge d'Affaires and lodged a formal protest —
against its own strategic partner, not against Iran.
This is unprecedented in the 102-day war.
India will raise this at the G7 in Evian-les-Bains (June 15-17).
A Modi-Trump bilateral is likely on the sidelines.
The Seamen Welfare Fund will pay ~Rs10 lakh to each bereaved family.

THE WIDER PICTURE — SAME 24 HOURS
US launched a 2nd night of strikes on Iran (Bandar Abbas, Sirik hit).
Iran retaliated at Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait.
An Iranian cargo ship sank in the Gulf of Oman (5 rescued).
IAEA board demands Iran declare its uranium stockpile.
Trump: Iran's military "completely defeated" — will "pay the price."
Yet a Qatari negotiating team is in Tehran. Diplomacy continues.

MARKETS
Nifty: 23,214.95 (-0.12%). Sensex: 73,983.18 (+0.09%) — gains pared.
Brent eased to $91 intraday, now climbing toward $95.
The Settebello deaths broke AFTER market close — Thursday will price it in.

FOR INDIA
This is no longer purely an energy/economic story.
562 Indian seafarers remain on 13 Indian-flagged vessels in the Gulf.
18,000+ Indian seafarers total in the region.
The blockade that was meant to pressure Iran has now killed Indians.
G7 (June 15-17) becomes a critical diplomatic moment.
Nifty support 23,000-23,100. Brent $95 = OMC pressure intensifies.
Watch for further MEA statements and any US response to the protest.
